title: A blockade runner disabled, tankers burning off Khasab, and missiles over Riyadh
summary: US forces disable the bulk carrier Huda as it tries to run the blockade, a tanker's crew abandons ship off Khasab and Iran claims three more tankers ablaze, Iran waves off Task Force Iron Gate, Russia hits Ukraine's grid and claims strikes on cargo ships near Odesa, Ukraine hits Oryol, and missile debris damages an Aramco building in Riyadh.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Sunday, November eighth. And the waters around Hormuz had one of their busiest days in a while.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's start with the US blockade. Central Command says its forces disabled a bulk carrier called the Huda in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday. It's flagged in Saint Kitts and Nevis.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And Central Command says the ship made several attempts to get through the blockade of Iranian ports before it was disabled.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Then, near the strait itself, the British maritime agency UKMTO said military authorities reported a tanker on fire about eight nautical miles northwest of Khasab, in Oman. The crew abandoned ship. There's no word yet on their condition or the ship's.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And the same night, another tanker was hit by an unknown projectile while heading out through the strait. All of its crew are accounted for.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Today, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three more oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the strait. As always, UKMTO hasn't confirmed the mine claims. And it says most ships now don't report incidents at all, so the true count could be higher.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the politics, Iran's military dismissed the new US task force, Iron Gate, as, quote, word play. That's the one meant to choke off Iran's land routes and the Caspian Sea.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the Wall Street Journal reports President Trump's advisers are divided. Some want to resume strikes on Iran. Others want to keep negotiating. Meanwhile the New York Times says thousands of US air and naval forces are positioned to resume major combat if he orders it.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So the same tension we've been tracking all week. Talks, minor strikes, and a much bigger option sitting in the background.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's go to Ukraine. Russia kept up its attacks on the power grid overnight.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The energy company DTEK says an attack on energy facilities in the Dnipropetrovsk region left more than six hundred thousand people without electricity. Russia says it hit substations there and in the Zhytomyr region.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Russia's defence ministry also says it struck three cargo ships near Odesa and Chornomorsk, on the Black Sea. Ukraine hadn't commented when that was reported.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And there's more detail on Friday night's big attack on Kyiv, the one that hit the Northern Bridge. Russia now says its targets included the bridge, a plant it says makes Flamingo cruise missiles, and power and munitions sites.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Remind people of the scale of that one.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Ukrainian officials said Russia launched a hundred and seventy-two drones and thirty-six ballistic missiles. Several missiles hit the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro, and it was closed. One person was killed and eight were wounded in the Kyiv area, and one more person was killed in the Dnipropetrovsk region.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the Flamingo plant claim is Russia's description. Ukraine hasn't confirmed what, if anything, was hit there. Ukraine kept striking back. Its General Staff says it hit targets in the Oryol, Saratov and Rostov regions on Friday night. That includes a factory in Oryol, hit with a Neptune missile, and the Saratov refinery we mentioned yesterday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the front line, the General Staff reported a hundred and ninety-nine clashes on Saturday. The busiest front was Kostiantynivka, with twenty-three Russian attacks. And the Institute for the Study of War says Russian attacks near Lyman didn't gain ground.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: All of this is a couple of days before the US, Russia and Ukraine meet again in Abu Dhabi, on Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now, the war between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia. Early this morning, Saudi Arabia says it intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh and other areas.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Falling debris damaged a building owned by the state oil company Aramco, in Riyadh's financial district. Saudi authorities said the impact was minimal.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The Houthis hadn't claimed that particular attack when it was reported. But on Saturday they said they carried out six missile and drone operations against Saudi oil sites and Riyadh's main airport.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And they say they're responding to Saudi airstrikes that, by their account, have killed dozens of civilians. None of those claims, on either side, has been independently verified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Some context from earlier in the week. On Saturday, Houthi-affiliated media said the death toll from a Saudi strike in Sanaa province had risen to twenty-two. That figure hasn't been verified either.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And on Thursday, the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a Houthi missile aimed at Medina. The Houthis didn't claim that one.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: A quick look at the other conflicts on the map. In southern Lebanon, the Israeli army carried out artillery shelling and a demolition in the village of Bani Haiyyan on Saturday. No casualties were reported.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That follows Israeli strikes on Kfar Tebnit and al-Mansouri on Thursday. And in Gaza, rescue services said Israeli strikes and gunfire killed five people on Thursday, including a woman and a twelve-year-old boy.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And in Sudan's war, the latest item on the map is from Wednesday. Ethiopia expelled six Sudanese diplomats after Sudan accused it, at the UN Security Council and the African Union, of hosting drone launch sites for the Rapid Support Forces.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Also, if you missed it, there's now a special video briefing on the ForceFinder site, covering the Western Hemisphere. Mexico's cartels, El Salvador, Haiti, Venezuela, Cuba and Nicaragua. It's in the sidebar under Video briefings.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the ships, no new fleet reports today, so the map hasn't changed. Two carriers, the George Washington and the George H. W. Bush, are still reported in the Arabian Sea supporting operations against Iran. The Eisenhower and the Nimitz are underway in the Atlantic, the Eisenhower in pre-deployment work-ups. And the Theodore Roosevelt was last reported in the South China Sea.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The next USNI fleet tracker is due tomorrow, Monday. It should show whether the Roosevelt has moved on, and whether there's any change in the Arabian Sea.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, what to watch. Whether the attacks on shipping keep spreading, and what the Huda episode means for blockade enforcement. Tuesday's talks in Abu Dhabi. And Trump's decision on whether to resume major strikes on Iran.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
